title: Vocal Jazz: line-check the wireless mics
about: First gameplay slice (PRODUCT_DESIGN.md sections 46 and 94): one signal chain (handheld -> receiver -> X32 input), one fault (a handheld powered on but muted), one objective that completes only on verified evidence, one hint ladder, one debrief. Everything marked tentative or unknown below is a placeholder to field-calibrate, not room truth.

clock.status: tentative: 4:50 doors / 5:00 rehearsal come from PRODUCT_DESIGN section 40; the per-action and per-move seconds are placeholders (section 89 says movement-time scaling is field-calibrate)

setup.status: scenario sizing chosen for a short slice, not a claim about how many mics Vocal Jazz uses
setup.note: X32 and receivers start powered on so that the transmitter mute is the only fault (one fault per section 94).

roles.value: This slice is the battery-in check at FOH (A2 alone, next to receivers and X32). The official line check is later, on stage: musicians make sound, the A1 confirms each channel at the X32.

ptu6000-rx.label: Phenyx Pro PTU-6000 receivers
ptu6000-rx.unknown: whether a muted transmitter still shows RF on the receiver. Only audio present / absent is modelled.
ptu6000-rx.units_status: current fact (owner, 2026-09-27): each receiver unit is 8 channels, top unit = 1-8, next = 9-16, and so on

devices_status: Owner, 2026-09-27: mics are named by windscreen colour then ring colour, and that is how people mostly refer to them (black red = 1, black orange = 2, black black = 7, black grey = 8, grey red = 9, grey orange = 10, grey black = 15, grey grey = 16). Ring order (owner-confirmed): red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, black, grey. Mics 17-24: treat as no windscreen for now (owner, 2026-09-27; may change). Handhelds live in the FOH mic drawer (manifest row IMG_4127).

mute_survives_power_cycle.status: current fact (owner, 2026-09-27): switching a muted mic off and on clears the mute

muted_indication.value: the handheld's display shows that it is muted
muted_indication.status: fact that it shows (owner, 2026-09-27); the exact glyph (speaker-with-slash icon, or the word MUTE) is unconfirmed. Needs a real mic graphic.

connections_status: Current fact (owner, 2026-09-27): handheld N -> receiver channel N -> X32 input N, over handheld -> PTU-6000 -> XLR -> X32 local analog input (PRODUCT_DESIGN section 37).

fault.label: A wireless handheld is powered on but muted
fault.target: one handheld in play, chosen by the seed

objective.label: Line-check the wireless mics
objective.goal: Every mic in play is verified: talking into it shows signal at its X32 input.
objective.source: PRODUCT_DESIGN sections 45 (speak into each mic), 55 (goals, not recipes; complete only after verification)

hints.text: No signal is reaching the receiver. Where could the problem be upstream?
The transmitter is muted. Unmute it and verify signal.
